pages.text: "Lolo is always first!" Riri in her yellow hat plopped down on the pier. Running and splashing like Lolo, she had slipped. Wet sand covered her knees.
Riri wanted to be fast and brave like Lolo. Farther away, Lolo carried armfuls of rope. "I am just slow. I am not good at anything." Her shoulders drooped.
Dad's motorboat bobbed, tied to the pier post. Even when Lolo jumped aboard, Riri did not look. She pulled her yellow hat low and kicked at the ground.
Dad the fisherman left his net and sat beside her. "Our Riri, what is worrying you?" Sniffling, she shared what was in her heart. "I cannot do things like Lolo."
Dad spread a big net over Riri's knees. "Then could you help me with one job? This net has a hole." Lolo climbed down and glanced at it. "No hole. It all looks the same."
Riri followed the net's spaces with a finger, row by row. After a while, her finger stopped. "Here! One hole." A little farther, she stopped again. "Another here. Two!"
Dad looked up at Riri. "You found what neither Lolo nor Dad saw. Lolo is quick—that is Lolo. And Riri—" Riri lifted her chin. "Riri is wonderful as Riri!"
Dad threaded a needle and stitched the holes neatly. In the next rows, Riri found two more tiny holes. Her smile stretched right up to her cheeks.
Now all three worked side by side. Strong Lolo pulled up the net, sharp-eyed Riri pointed out holes, and Dad mended them. "Quick Lolo, sharp-eyed Riri!" Lolo called. Riri is wonderful as Riri!
When the lighthouse lit up, Dad lifted Riri high. Being quick and seeing well were different gifts. "Our Riri has the sharpest eyes. Riri is wonderful as Riri!" Dad said.
